description: This course covers fundamental algorithm design techniques including greedy algorithms, dynamic programming, and divide-and-conquer strategies; analysis of time and space complexity using Big-O notation; data structures such as heaps, balanced trees, and graphs; and standard algorithms like Dijkstra's shortest path, Kruskal's minimum spanning tree, and the Fast Fourier Transform. Topics include sorting algorithms (merge sort, quick sort, heap sort), algorithmic paradigms (backtracking, branch and bound), and algorithm optimization using memoization and caching. The course also explores algorithmic standards such as the IEEE 754 floating-point standard and the use of computational tools like Python and C++ for algorithm implementation and testing.

clos.text: Define the time and space complexity of algorithms using Big-O notation.
Describe the characteristics of different algorithmic paradigms such as greedy, dynamic programming, and divide-and-conquer.
Explain the principles of data structures such as heaps, balanced trees, and graphs and their applications in algorithm design.
Apply standard algorithms such as Dijkstra's, Kruskal's, and the Fast Fourier Transform to solve computational problems.
Implement and evaluate the efficiency of algorithms using Python and C++ for real-world applications.

topics: Introduction to Algorithms and Complexity Analysis
Data Structures: Arrays, Lists, and Trees
Graph Algorithms and Shortest Path Techniques
Advanced Data Structures: Heaps and Balanced Trees
